CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFPROCRESULT

A stored procedure returns one result set for each SELECT it runs. Each CFPROCRESULT inside a CFSTOREDPROC turns one of them into an ordinary query variable that you can use with CFOUTPUT, CFLOOP and the query functions.

Category

Database manipulation

Syntax

<CFPROCRESULT NAME="query_name"
    RESULTSET="1-n"
    MAXROWS="maxrows">

Attributes

NAME
Required. Name of the query that receives the result set.
RESULTSET
Optional, default "1". Which result set to take, counting from 1.
MAXROWS
Optional. Maximum number of rows to keep.

Usage

Result sets are numbered in the order the procedure produces them, including those of procedures it calls with EXEC. If the procedure returns fewer result sets than RESULTSET asks for, the query variable is not created; test for it with IsDefined before you use it.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSTOREDPROC PROCEDURE="CountByDept" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
  <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="In" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_VARCHAR" VALUE="Engineering">
  <CFPROCPARAM TYPE="Out" CFSQLTYPE="CF_SQL_INTEGER" VARIABLE="Total">
  <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Depts" RESULTSET="1">
  <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Offices" RESULTSET="2" MAXROWS="1">
  <CFPROCRESULT NAME="Third" RESULTSET="3">
</CFSTOREDPROC>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Engineering has #Total# employees and a payroll of #DollarFormat(Depts.Payroll)#.
It is based in #Offices.Location#.</P>
<P>IsDefined("Third"): #IsDefined("Third")# (CountByDept returns two result sets).</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

<!--- The same procedure's first result set, through CFQUERY --->
<CFQUERY NAME="ViaQuery" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
EXEC CountByDept @Department = 'Sales', @Total = NULL
</CFQUERY>
<CFOUTPUT QUERY="ViaQuery"><P>Via CFQUERY: #Department#, #Employees# employees.</P></CFOUTPUT>
